concepts.def: A tiny nucleus of protons and neutrons with electrons in shells.
Types of nuclear radiation with different penetration and ionising power.
Time for half the undecayed nuclei to decay.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Nuclear Physics — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Nuclear Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Nuclear Physics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which type of radiation is stopped by a sheet of paper?
options: X-rays
Alpha
Beta
Gamma
No neutrons at all.
The same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Different numbers of protons but the same neutrons.
The same mass number always.

mcqs.q: In the nuclide notation ²³⁸₉₂U, the number 92 is:
options: The proton (atomic) number
The number of neutrons
The mass number
The number of energy levels
Caused by chemical reactions.
A random, spontaneous process unaffected by temperature or pressure.
Triggered by heating the sample.
Predictable for each individual nucleus.

mcqs.q: After two half-lives, how much of a radioactive sample remains undecayed?
options: Yes — heating the sample sets the decay time.
None — two halves means it has all decayed.
Three quarters of the sample.
One quarter — each half-life halves whatever is left.

mcqs.q: Is food that has been irradiated to sterilise it radioactive afterwards?
options: No — irradiation transfers energy but no radioactive material; contamination is what makes things radioactive.
Yes — heating the sample sets the decay time.
Yes — anything exposed to radiation becomes radioactive.
Yes — but only food in metal cans.

mcqs.q: Can you predict when an individual nucleus will decay?
options: Three quarters of the sample.
No — decay is random; only the average behaviour of large numbers of nuclei is predictable, via the half-life.
Yes — heating the sample sets the decay time.
Yes — each nucleus decays exactly when one half-life has passed.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Half-life”?
options: Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
The time taken for half the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay, or for the activity to fall by half.
A helium nucleus (2 protons and 2 neutrons); strongly ionising but stopped by paper or skin.
The tiny central core of the atom, containing protons and neutrons and holding nearly all the atom's mass.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Alpha particle”?
options: The time taken for half the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay, or for the activity to fall by half.
The tiny central core of the atom, containing protons and neutrons and holding nearly all the atom's mass.
A helium nucleus (2 protons and 2 neutrons); strongly ionising but stopped by paper or skin.
A fast electron emitted when a neutron in the nucleus changes into a proton; stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Isotopes”?
options: A fast electron emitted when a neutron in the nucleus changes into a proton; stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium.
The tiny central core of the atom, containing protons and neutrons and holding nearly all the atom's mass.
The time taken for half the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay, or for the activity to fall by half.
Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Nucleus”?
options: A helium nucleus (2 protons and 2 neutrons); strongly ionising but stopped by paper or skin.
The tiny central core of the atom, containing protons and neutrons and holding nearly all the atom's mass.
The time taken for half the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay, or for the activity to fall by half.
High-frequency electromagnetic radiation emitted from the nucleus; weakly ionising but highly penetrating.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Beta particle”?
options: The tiny central core of the atom, containing protons and neutrons and holding nearly all the atom's mass.
Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
The time taken for half the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay, or for the activity to fall by half.
A fast electron emitted when a neutron in the nucleus changes into a proton; stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Gamma radiation”?
options: A helium nucleus (2 protons and 2 neutrons); strongly ionising but stopped by paper or skin.
The time taken for half the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay, or for the activity to fall by half.
The tiny central core of the atom, containing protons and neutrons and holding nearly all the atom's mass.
High-frequency electromagnetic radiation emitted from the nucleus; weakly ionising but highly penetrating.

mcqs.q: A sample's activity is 800 Bq and its half-life is 10 minutes. What is the activity after 20 minutes?
options: 100 Bq
0 Bq
200 Bq
400 Bq

free_texts.hint: It's one of the six key terms above.

sequence.term: Alpha particles fired at gold foil

A concentrated positive charge repels them
Roughly 1 in 8000 return toward the source
Rutherford: a tiny, dense, positive nucleus
